**Confirmatory Adaptive Clinical Trial Design and Analysis**

`rpact` supports the design, simulation, and analysis of confirmatory clinical
trials, from standard fixed-sample planning to group sequential and adaptive
methods. Sample size and power planning and simulation are available for
continuous, binary, survival (time-to-event), and count data endpoints.

## Functional Range

### Sample size and power planning

* Standard fixed-sample designs without interim analyses
* Classical group sequential designs with planned interim analyses
* Sample size and power calculations for
    + means (continuous endpoints)
    + rates (binary endpoints)
    + survival (time-to-event) endpoints with flexible recruitment and
      survival-time options
    + count data endpoints

### Simulation and adaptive trial design

* Power and operating-characteristic simulations for means, rates, survival
  data, and count data
* Assessment of adaptive sample size or event-number reassessment based on
  conditional power
* Multi-stage adaptive hypothesis testing based on the combination testing
  principle
* Assessment of treatment selection strategies in multi-arm trials, including
  multi-arm multi-stage (MAMS) settings for means, rates, and survival endpoints
* Simulation and analysis methods for population enrichment designs with means,
  rates, and hazard ratios

### Analysis and trial conduct

* Confirmatory analysis for means and rates in one-arm and two-arm trials,
  and for survival endpoints in treatment comparisons
* Multi-arm and population enrichment analysis for means, rates, and survival
  endpoints
* Analysis of general estimates and standard errors supplied through
  `getDataset(est = ..., se = ...)`
* Support for fixed-sample designs, classical group sequential designs, and
  adaptive multi-arm multi-stage (MAMS) designs based on the inverse normal or
  Fisher combination test
* Automatic boundary recalculation during a trial using alpha-spending
  approaches, including under- and over-running

## Learn to use rpact

We recommend three ways to learn how to use `rpact`:

> 1. Use RPACT Cloud:
>    [demo.rpact.cloud](https://demo.rpact.cloud)
> 2. Use the Vignettes:
>    [rpact.org/vignettes](https://www.rpact.org/vignettes/)

>    [rpact.com](https://www.rpact.com/services/learning-and-training/)

### RPACT Cloud 

**RPACT Cloud** provides guided, browser-based access to selected `rpact`
functionality, including study design, sample size calculation, simulation,
and reporting, without requiring users to write R code:
[demo.rpact.cloud](https://demo.rpact.cloud).

### Vignettes and function reference

Practical examples and tutorials are available at
[rpact.org/vignettes](https://www.rpact.org/vignettes/).
For function arguments, return values, and examples, see the
[function reference](https://docs.rpact.org).

## User Concept

### Workflow

1. Create a fixed-sample, group sequential, or adaptive design.
2. Compare alternative designs with `getDesignSet()`.
3. Calculate the required sample size with, for example, `getSampleSizeMeans()`,
   or evaluate power for a specified sample size with `getPowerMeans()`.
4. Assess operating characteristics and adaptation strategies using simulation,
   for example, `getSimulationMeans()`.
5. Prepare aggregated trial data with `getDataset()` and analyze them with
   `getAnalysisResults()`.

### Planning example

Plan a two-arm trial with a continuous endpoint, a one-sided significance level
of 0.025, 90% power, and three analyses at 50%, 75%, and 100% of the planned
information. Assume a mean difference of 0.5 and a common standard deviation of 1.

```{r planning, message=FALSE}
library(rpact)
design <- getDesignGroupSequential(
    kMax = 3, informationRates = c(0.5, 0.75, 1),
    alpha = 0.025, beta = 0.1, sided = 1, typeOfDesign = "OF"
)
sampleSize <- getSampleSizeMeans(
    design = design, groups = 2, alternative = 0.5,
    stDev = 1, allocationRatioPlanned = 1
)
summary(sampleSize)
```

For a design without interim analyses, use `getDesignFixed()` instead.

### Analysis example

The following illustrative data represent two independent groups at each of
three stages. Sample sizes, means, and standard deviations are **stage-wise**:
each entry describes only the new observations collected in that stage.
The sample sizes are chosen for illustration, independently of the planning
result above.

```{r analysis}
trialData <- getDataset(
    sampleSizes1 = c(40, 20, 20), sampleSizes2 = c(40, 20, 20),
    means1 = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.5), means2 = c(0, 0, 0),
    stDevs1 = c(1, 1, 1), stDevs2 = c(1, 1, 1)
)
analysisResults <- getAnalysisResults(
    design = design, dataInput = trialData, directionUpper = TRUE
)
summary(analysisResults)
```

If the available summaries are cumulative, use the corresponding `cumulative`
prefixes, such as `cumulativeSampleSizes1`, `cumulativeMeans1`, and
`cumulativeStDevs1`. For survival data, cumulative event counts and log-rank
statistics are commonly used; see `getDataset()` for the required inputs.
Analysis results and the availability of confidence intervals depend on the
chosen design and endpoint; see `getAnalysisResults()` for details.

### Focus on Usability

The terms *survival* and *time-to-event* refer to the same endpoint type here.
The corresponding function names use the suffix `Survival`.

The most important [rpact](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rpact) functions
have intuitive names:

-   `getDesign`[`Fixed`/`GroupSequential`/`InverseNormal`/`Fisher`]`()`
-   [`getDesignCharacteristics()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getDesignCharacteristics.html)
-   `getSampleSize`[`Means`/`Rates`/`Survival`/`Counts`]`()`
-   `getPower`[`Means`/`Rates`/`Survival`/`Counts`]`()`
-   `getSimulation`[`Means`/`Rates`/`Survival`/`Counts`]`()`
-   `getSimulationMultiArm`[`Means`/`Rates`/`Survival`]`()`
-   `getSimulationEnrichment`[`Means`/`Rates`/`Survival`]`()`
-   `getDesignConditionalDunnett()` for adaptive two-stage multi-arm designs
-   [`getDataset()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getDataset.html)
-   [`getAnalysisResults()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getAnalysisResults.html)
-   [`getStageResults()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getStageResults.html)

[RStudio](https://posit.co/downloads/) / [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/)
/ [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) / [Eclipse](https://www.eclipse.org):
auto code completion makes it easy to use these functions.

### R generics

Result objects support familiar R functions such as `print()`, `summary()`,
`plot()`, `as.data.frame()`, `names()`, and `length()`. The available methods
depend on the object class; see the corresponding function reference.

### Utilities

Several utility functions are available, e.g.

-   [`getAccrualTime()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getAccrualTime.html)
-   [`getPiecewiseSurvivalTime()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getPiecewiseSurvivalTime.html)
-   [`getNumberOfSubjects()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getNumberOfSubjects.html)
-   [`getEventProbabilities()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/getEventProbabilities.html)
-   [`getPiecewiseExponentialDistribution()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/utilitiesForPiecewiseExponentialDistribution.html)
-   survival helper functions for conversion of `pi`, `lambda` and `median`,
    e.g.,
    [`getLambdaByMedian()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/utilitiesForSurvivalTrials.html)
-   [`testPackage()`](https://docs.rpact.org/reference/testPackage.html):
    installation qualification on a client computer or company server (see
    [Installation Qualification of
    rpact](https://www.rpact.org/vignettes/utilities/rpact_installation_qualification/))

## Validation

For organizations using `rpact` in FDA/GxP-regulated environments, RPACT offers
support and formal validation documentation for use on validated corporate
computer systems. The documentation can be customized and licensed for exclusive
use by your company to support applicable regulatory requirements.

The validation documentation also contains the personal access data required to
run the full test suite for installation qualification with `testPackage()`.

> [Contact RPACT](https://www.rpact.com/contact/) to learn more.

## RPACT Connect

**RPACT Connect** provides access to insights, downloads, and premium support
for users and organizations working with RPACT software:
[connect.rpact.app](https://connect.rpact.app).

## About

**rpact** is free of charge and open source, licensed under
[LGPL-3](https://cran.r-project.org/web/licenses/LGPL-3). It implements a broad
range of methods described in the monograph by
[Wassmer and Brannath (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-89669-9).
Formal validation documentation is available to customers and supporting
members through the
[RPACT service level agreement](https://www.rpact.com/services/service-level-agreement/).

**RPACT GmbH** develops **Statistical Tools for Drug Development**.
We develop and support R packages, Shiny applications, and cloud-based tools
for clinical research, with services covering software development, validation,
technical support, consulting, and training.

Our products include [rpact](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rpact) and
[RPACT Cloud](https://demo.rpact.cloud). We also maintain and support
[crmPack](https://www.rpact.com/products/r-package-crmpack/), the open-source
package for dose escalation trial design, simulation, and analysis.

For more information, visit [www.rpact.com](https://www.rpact.com).
